_comment: Professional audiences used by the `who_uses_it` field. Tool entries must reference `name` (or an `alias`); unknown values fail the build. The /roles/<slug>/ pages are generated from this file plus the tool data, so they can never drift out of sync.

roles.name: Software Engineers
roles.blurb: Write, review and debug code, and increasingly supervise the agents that produce the first pass of it.

roles.name: DevOps & Platform Engineers
roles.blurb: Wire AI into CI/CD, incident response and internal platforms, with cost and access controls that hold up in production.

roles.name: Engineering Managers
roles.blurb: Decide what the team is allowed to paste into a model, and measure whether the assisted version of the work is actually better.

roles.name: Data Scientists
roles.blurb: Prototype models, build evaluation sets and keep experiments reproducible enough to hand over.

roles.name: Data Analysts
roles.blurb: Turn natural-language questions into governed queries, then defend the definitions behind the chart.

roles.name: Product Managers
roles.blurb: Synthesise research, write the specs, and keep stakeholder updates fast but honest.

roles.name: Designers
roles.blurb: Explore interface directions quickly and hand off something engineers can actually build against.

roles.name: Marketers
roles.blurb: Produce campaign variants at volume without losing the brand voice, then measure what moved.

roles.name: Writers & Editors
roles.blurb: Get past the blank page faster than you would alone, then edit hard - the value is judgement, not word count.

roles.name: Customer Support
roles.blurb: Answer tickets faster with grounded suggestions, and know exactly when the assistant should hand over to a human.

roles.name: Sales
roles.blurb: Research accounts, prep calls and keep CRM notes accurate without spending the afternoon on it.

roles.name: Recruiters
roles.blurb: Source and screen at volume while staying inside the rules on automated decisions about candidates.

roles.name: HR & People Ops
roles.blurb: Answer policy questions consistently, draft employee communications and keep people data tidy.

roles.name: Finance
roles.blurb: Close faster and model scenarios, with a paper trail an auditor can follow.

roles.name: Legal
roles.blurb: Review and draft contracts at speed while keeping both the citation trail and privilege intact.

roles.name: Operations
roles.blurb: Remove the manual hops between systems and keep the process documented when someone leaves.

roles.name: Project Managers
roles.blurb: Turn meetings and messy threads into plans, owners and dates that survive contact with reality.

roles.name: Executives & Founders
roles.blurb: Get to a defensible first answer before the meeting, and sanity-check the numbers the team brings.

roles.name: Consultants
roles.blurb: Compress research and slide production so more of the budget goes to the thinking.

roles.name: Researchers
roles.blurb: Find and read the literature faster, with citations you can verify rather than trust.

roles.name: Educators
roles.blurb: Build materials and differentiated exercises for mixed classrooms without a second workday.

roles.name: Students
roles.blurb: Learn concepts on demand - with the caveat that outsourcing the thinking defeats the purpose.

roles.name: IT Administrators
roles.blurb: Provision and constrain AI tools across an organisation, and keep a record of who has access to what.

roles.name: Security & Risk Engineers
roles.blurb: Find the data-leak paths in AI adoption before an auditor, a regulator or an attacker does.
